findings: Reciprocal adjacency connection uses the supplied shared vertex to select slots; the low-level helper does not require an additional shared-edge test.
Triangle deletion preserves the destination record identity, disconnects matching reciprocal pointers and moves the last record into the hole.
Three-edge repair reverses supplied boundary records; all-one-triangle loops remove a triangle, all-distinct cases append a cap, and mixed or repeated-vertex cases do not append.
The appended cap uses Float32 differences, products and normalization; this differs from the source face-normal worker.
Boundary-tree erasure detaches a successor, rebalances and copies its payload into the selected node. Root-seeded traversal must follow the resulting tree.
A reserved invalid destination is erased but not appended to the walk. The initial test using it as an ordinary high identifier failed; that attempt remains retained.
analyticIntegration: A three-side tetrahedron fixture with supplied reciprocal adjacency closes its triangular opening, with every resulting edge linked reciprocally in opposite directions.
Compaction and vertex-normal generation accept the repaired tetrahedron and produce finite unit vertex normals within the fixture tolerance.
An isolated triangle is removed and compaction drops its orphan positions.
A quad retains its four-edge boundary; it is not fed into the three-edge helper.
Duplicate directed boundary keys retain the first inserted triangle record.
remaining: Resolve and port the native virtual adjacency builder; analytic integration currently supplies its links explicitly.
Verify coordinator lifetime semantics for pre-collected triangle pointers when deletion moves records.
Resolve exact-lattice behavior, source preparation, mutable initializer and parallel frontiers.
Integrate a complete shared GUI/MCP reconstruction operation and validate original/native geometry, history, cancellation, saved projects and rendered output.
limitations: Synthetic explicit topology and historical static bytes; no fresh native runtime output or original-scan acceptance.
Tree NIL-black behavior follows the recovered balancing invariants; allocation/pool layout and full native metadata are not modeled.
The private triangle-index and boundary-length guards are validation safeguards, not established native GUI admission rules.
